answers.documents: $language is the sky_locale's first letter x 100 + its second letter, with de=405, fr=618, en=514, es=519.
answers.verbatim: # language variable is the sky_locale first_letter x 100 + second_letter - de=405 fr=618 en=514 es=519 ...
answers.code_check: src/coreModule/core.cpp:2214-2223 Core::setLanguage(): for each of the first two letters it finds j in 1..26 with lang[i]==j+96 and folds language = language*100 + j. So a=1..z=26: d=4,e=5 -> 405; f=6,r=18 -> 618; e=5,n=14 -> 514; e=5,s=19 -> 519. ALL FOUR EXAMPLES CORRECT. (A letter outside a-z yields 27; a locale shorter than 2 characters reads lang[1] past the end.)

divergences.claim: 'z_reflection is used when the object has symetry' - that setting z_reflection changes how the volumetric object is drawn.
divergences.code_says: The value is looked up and then thrown away by a typo: `it->second == "true";` is an equality COMPARISON whose result is discarded, not an assignment. z_reflection is therefore always false, so VolumObj3D::reconstruct never sets texCoef.z=2 and never ORs PS_ZREFLECT into the pipeline selection.
divergences.code_anchor: src/inGalaxyModule/dsoNavigator.cpp:303-306 (bool z_reflection = false; auto it = args.find("z_reflection"); if (it != args.end()) it->second == "true";) and the consumer src/coreModule/volumObj3D.cpp:230-233
divergences.why: The `== / =` typo makes this look like an engine defect rather than a doc error, and the doc line is valuable precisely because it states the INTENT that the code cannot: 'used when the object has symetry' is exactly what texCoef.z=2 plus PS_ZREFLECT would do (mirror the volume about z). This ANSWERS the previously open gap G-DSO3D-1 ('read and discarded; intended behaviour unknown') and simultaneously pins the defect.

divergences.claim: 'Usual tex are 512x512 - Default rate is the width' - that when `rate` is omitted it defaults to the texture's width.
divergences.code_says: The default is the hard-coded constant 512, not the texture width: rayPoints = (_rayPoints) ? _rayPoints : 512. A 256- or 1024-wide texture still gets 512 ray samples.
divergences.why: The claim is true for the 512x512 textures the same sentence calls 'usual', and the code comment one line below (volumObj3D.cpp:229 'Assume width and height are equal') shows the author had the same width-based model in mind, so this may be intent that was never implemented. It is false for any other texture size, which is the case a reader would hit.

divergences.claim: 'Put brightness of Algol to minimum of brightness m2.1/m3.4 = 0.62 (1 is normal brightness)' with `illuminate hp 14576 size 0.62 display on` - that a size between 0 and 1 scales the star's brightness.
divergences.code_says: For 0 < size <= 1 the engine only un-hides the star and removes any illuminate, then returns: no magnitude is touched. The code that would do exactly what the doc describes - addVariableStar with magMax = magMin = mag * _size - is present but COMMENTED OUT.

The neighbouring claim on line 745 (size 0 = discard the star) IS live - see answers.

divergences.claim: Two prose lines beginning '(Warning! Don't forget to put a wait duration 0.01 ...' at lines 940 and 945, written as documentation.
divergences.code_says: Neither line starts with '#', so the script loader turns both into tokens and the parser executes them. The command becomes '(warning!' (lower-cased), which is in no command table, so each produces an unknown-command error plus a Levenshtein did-you-mean, twice per run of the file.
divergences.code_anchor: src/scriptModule/script.cpp:117 (a line is kept as a command whenever line[0] != '#' && != 0 && != '\r' && != '\n') and src/interfaceModule/app_command_interface.cpp:160-161 (first token lower-cased into `command`)
divergences.why: This is a NEW instance of the class that divergence D-INDENT described, introduced by this revision - and it arrived in the same edit that FIXED D-INDENT (the two indented '#' comments at old lines 1269/1271 are now at column 0). A sweep of the whole current file finds exactly these two lines as non-comment lines whose first token is not a registered command; prefixing each with '#' is the whole fix. Note that INLINE '#' comments on command lines (used heavily in the new lines 37-46) are safe: app_command_interface.cpp:128-141 strips a '#' outside quotes before parsing.

divergences.claim: '# Start video paused (forcing preloading)' with `media videoname ... action play pause on` - that `pause on` starts the video paused.
divergences.code_says: The paused flag is read with Utility::strToBool, which returns true ONLY for 'true' or '1' (case-insensitively). 'on' is not accepted, so paused is false and the video starts playing normally. Writing `pause true` or `pause 1` would work.
divergences.code_anchor: src/interfaceModule/app_command_interface.cpp:3625 (bool paused = Utility::strToBool(args[W_PAUSE], false);) and src/tools/utility.cpp:432-438 (only "true" or "1")
divergences.why: The trap is that the neighbouring key on the same command uses a DIFFERENT converter: `loop on` works because :3626-3631 uses Utility::isTrue, which does accept 'on' (src/tools/utility.hpp:160-171). Two adjacent keys of the same command disagree about what 'on' means, and the doc's example landed on the side that loses. Either the doc line should read `pause true`, or :3625 should use isTrue like the rest of the command; that choice is the owner's.

divergences.claim: '# Play SRT within a video' with a `media subtitlename ... videoname ... type VIEWPORT audioname ...` line - that this line plays the video with its subtitles.
divergences.code_says: The line has no `action`, so commandMedia skips the entire play block (which is where subtitlename, subtitle_project, videoname, type and audioname are read) and falls through to the standalone subtitle branch, which only calls playerSetShowSubtitles(true) and returns SUCCESS. No srt is loaded, no video is played, and nothing reports a problem.
divergences.code_anchor: src/interfaceModule/app_command_interface.cpp:3621-3624 (the whole block is gated on a non-empty `action`) vs the fall-through at :3891-3900; the srt loader that is skipped is at :3683-3738
divergences.why: Adding `action play` to the line makes it do what the comment says. All four keys the line uses are real and registered; only the missing `action` disarms them. This is a fresh instance of the silent-success class already recorded as D-CONFMOD (a well-formed line that reports SUCCESS while doing almost nothing).

divergences.claim: '# jump to any mode (in_solarsystem in_stellarsystem in_galaxy in_universe in_sandbox)' and the worked line `mode jump in_sandbox`.
divergences.code_says: Executor::switchMode has no branch for in_sandbox (or insandbox), and the Executor holds no sandbox module at all. The call still runs currentMode->onExit(), clears the selection, and runs currentMode->onEnter() on the SAME mode - so the observer stays where it was, loses its selection, and the command reports success.
divergences.code_anchor: src/executorModule/executor.cpp:80-104 (the four accepted values are ingalaxy/in_galaxy, inuniverse/in_universe, insolarsystem/in_solarsystem, instellarsystem/in_stellarsystem, with an unconditional onExit/onEnter around them); reached from src/interfaceModule/app_command_interface.cpp:3596-3598
divergences.why: in_sandbox is a real engine token elsewhere - src/interfaceModule/app_command_interface.cpp:4083 accepts it as a `body action load mode` value, src/ojmModule/ojm_mgr.cpp:50-51 maps it to STATE_POSITION::IN_SANDBOX, and MODULE::IN_SANDBOX is enum value 4 (which the doc correctly documents at line 1546). So either the switchMode branch was never written or it was removed; the doc may be describing a mode that exists everywhere except at its entry point. Worth putting to the owner rather than deciding here. The other four values on line 1062 are all live.

divergences.claim: '# the ZHR value is indicative and not taken into account at the moment / # you have to use a "meteors zhr" command to make it effective' - that the zhr argument of `meteors day ... zhr N` does nothing.
divergences.code_says: It is taken into account. `meteors day D ... zhr N` stores N as the third component of that day's radiant, and on every update MeteorMgr compares the current day's radiant[2] against ZHR and, when they differ, calls setZHR with it - so on day D the stored value takes over the rate.
divergences.code_anchor: src/coreModule/meteor_mgr.cpp:102-106 (Vec3f radiant = Meteor::getRadiant(currentDayOfYear); if (radiant[2] != (float)ZHR) setZHR((int)radiant[2]);) with the store at src/coreModule/meteor.hpp:51-53 and the reverse coupling at src/coreModule/meteor_mgr.hpp:55-59 (setZHR also writes the value into TODAY's radiant slot)
divergences.why: The tester's own hedge 'at the moment' says he expected this to change, and the shipped baseRadiant table (src/coreModule/meteor.cpp:51+) already carries per-day ZHR values in the third component, which only makes sense if that component is read. The practical consequence is the opposite of the doc's advice: a `meteors zhr X` issued while the date sits on a day that has a stored radiant ZHR will be overwritten on the next update.

divergences.claim: '# set the field of view by default when reseting with [Home] key' for `set init_fov 180`.
divergences.code_says: Pressing [Home] calls App::init(), which re-reads init_fov FROM THE CONFIG FILE into Core::InitFov and immediately applies it to the projection - so the scripted value is discarded, not used. What `set init_fov` really governs is the auto-zoom-out target used by `zoom auto out` / `zoom auto initial`.
divergences.code_anchor: src/uiModule/ui.cpp:2528-2531 ([Home] -> app->init() then queue internal/initial.sts), src/appModule/app.cpp:646 (core->init(conf)), src/coreModule/core.cpp:537-538 (InitFov = conf.getDouble(SCS_NAVIGATION, SCK_INIT_FOV); projection->setFov(InitFov);). The live consumer of a scripted value is src/coreModule/core.cpp:1436-1438 and :1484 (zoomToBothPaths(InitFov, ...)). The setter itself is src/coreModule/core.hpp:204.
divergences.why: The command is real and registered (app_command_init.cpp:345, handler app_command_interface.cpp:2347), and the installed internal/initial.sts that [Home] runs contains no zoom command at all, so nothing in that path re-applies the scripted FOV either. Whether [Home] SHOULD preserve a scripted init_fov is a product question, not a documentation one - hence undetermined rather than 'doc is wrong'.

divergences.claim: '# All faders to off in 1 second' with `transition action skip duration 1`.
divergences.code_says: The duration is in MILLISECONDS, not seconds. Core::update takes an int delta_time and divides by 1000 to get seconds, so `duration 1` advances the faders by 0.001 s - effectively nothing. One second would be `duration 1000`. (The default, when duration is absent, is 3600 ms = 3.6 s, which is what makes the plain `transition action skip` on line 1476 look instantaneous.)
divergences.code_anchor: src/interfaceModule/app_command_interface.cpp:4872-4880 (float duration = evalDouble(args[W_DURATION]); if (!duration) duration = 3600; ... stcore->update(duration)) and src/coreModule/core.cpp:2624-2626 (void Core::update(int delta_time) { ... const float deltaSeconds = delta_time / 1000.f; ...})
divergences.why: This is the first documentation the `transition` command has ever had, so the unit was never stated anywhere before; the open gap G-TRANS-1 records exactly this ambiguity ('the code answers milliseconds but the default 3600 is commented Ensure transitions complete now'). The new doc line resolves the ambiguity in the wrong direction. A second, smaller trap on the same path: `duration` is truncated to int by the call, so `duration 0.5` advances by 0 ms while still passing the !duration test.

divergences.claim: '# All faders to off for the preceding actions' for `transition action skip`.
divergences.code_says: `skip` does not set faders off; it runs the transition clock forward so every pending fade REACHES ITS TARGET at once. After `flag atmosphere on` followed by `transition action skip`, the atmosphere is fully ON, not off.
divergences.code_anchor: src/interfaceModule/app_command_interface.cpp:4871-4880 - the only thing `skip` does is force the transition flag on, call stcore->update(duration) and restore the flag; src/coreModule/core.cpp:2624-2626 advances CoreLink::update and transitions.update by that many seconds
divergences.why: The sentence is readable two ways - 'set the faders to off' (wrong) or 'turn the fading off, i.e. finish it now' (right) - and only the tester knows which he meant. Flagged rather than resolved because the first reading is the natural English one and would mislead.

divergences.claim: '# Create planet in in_stellar_system' / '# Create moon in in_stellar_system' with `body action load mode in_stellar_system ...` - that `mode` chooses which system the new body is created in.
divergences.code_says: For `body action load`, `mode` is only consulted to decide whether the line is an OJM/3D-model load; the three values tested are in_universe, in_galaxy and in_sandbox. Any other value - including this one - falls through and the body is added to whatever system is CURRENT, with the mode key silently dropped.
divergences.code_anchor: src/interfaceModule/app_command_interface.cpp:4080 (argMode = args["mode"]) and :4083 (the three-value test), then :4118-4124 which calls stcore->addSolarSystemBody(args) unconditionally; src/coreModule/core.cpp:832-835 -> src/bodyModule/ssystem_factory.cpp:827-829 (currentSystem->addBody(param))
divergences.why: The spelling makes it worse: `in_stellar_system` occurs NOWHERE in the engine (see new_surface) - the stellar-system token is `in_stellarsystem`/`instellarsystem`, and only Executor::switchMode knows it. So the two lines happen to work if and only if you are already standing in the 51Peg system, and the `mode` key contributes nothing. Whether `body action load mode <system>` SHOULD target a system is exactly the scope question the earlier pass deferred (gap G-BODY-1, 'body downstream vocabulary - deferred to INTENT item 4'), so this is evidence for that decision, not a bug report.

The RELATIVE claim was banked divergence D-SETHEAD and its removal is correct: APP_HEADING is a plain assignment, coreLink->setHeading(evalDouble(setValue)) at app_command_interface.cpp:2289-2290, so `set heading +15` jumps to 15, it does not add 15. But `set heading` itself is LIVE and registered (base_command_interface.hpp for ACP_SC_HEADING, app_command_init.cpp:309) and now occurs ZERO times in the file. Mitigation: the `heading azimuth` / `heading delta_azimuth` command, which is the properly-relative one (app_command_interface.cpp:2677-2688), is documented at lines 715-723, and old line 831's `set heading 90` inside the VR block was replaced by `heading azimuth 90 duration 3` at current line 952. So the FUNCTION is still documented; only the `set heading` spelling is not.

removed_lines.text: # This command permit to reset the timer to resynchronize after some images loading / # It'll wait automatically the time needed to load those images / wait action reset_timer (old lines 1364-1366)
removed_lines.note: CORRECT REMOVAL of banked divergence D-WAITRESET / SS-10. commandWait at HEAD (src/interfaceModule/app_command_interface.cpp:1488-1532) knows only `loading`, `duration` and `video_termination`; `action` reaches the final 'unrecognized or malformed argument name'. The intent is now served by the new `wait loading ...` family at lines 1555-1565.

removed_lines.text: # This permit to keep a panorama even after a lift-off (spacecraft argument) / image name zodfisheye ... spacecraft on action load (old lines 680-682)
removed_lines.note: HALF of banked divergence D-SPACECRAFT / SS-9 removed. commandImage never reads a `spacecraft` key (app_command_interface.cpp:3062-3222), so this half was dead. BUT the LANDSCAPE half survives at current lines 874-875 ('# Draw a landscape that will resist to take-off (as a spacecraft cockpit)' / `landscape ... spacecraft on action load`), and it is equally dead: a case-insensitive grep for 'spacecraft' over all of src/ (excluding the product name) returns only COMMENTED-OUT occurrences - src/bodyModule/body_decor.cpp:14,16,28,32,34 and src/coreModule/core.cpp:737. The divergence is therefore half-retired, half-live.

removed_lines.text: # Duplicate the image or video at 180<0xB0> if Twice and +120<0xB0> and -120<0xB0> if Thrice / image name zodiac action twice / image name zodiac action thrice (old lines 725-727)
removed_lines.note: FIX for banked divergence D-IMGTWICE, replaced by `project twice|thrice` on the load line at current lines 827-829 (app_command_interface.cpp:3093-3100). The dead `action twice` form nevertheless SURVIVES at current lines 974 and 1570, both inside the MEDIA section, so the divergence is not fully retired.

removed_lines.note: FIX for banked divergence D-INDENT / SS-7: both comments are now at column 0 (current lines 1421 and 1423), so script.cpp:117 classifies them as comments. A sweep of the whole current file finds no indented '#' line left.

unclear.tried: Read lines 837-864 in context. Line 840 is byte-identical to line 841 and both open the INITIALISATION block with no comment between them; commandClear (src/interfaceModule/app_command_interface.cpp:2595-2662) is idempotent so the duplicate is harmless. I could find no fact the second copy documents and no comment attached to it, so I cannot tell whether it is deliberate (e.g. belt-and-braces before a show) or an editing accident. Worth one question to the tester rather than a guess.

Read lines 1542-1552. The block opens a `struct if` and no `struct if end` follows before the WAIT section. app_command_interface.cpp:197-200 shows the engine now reports exactly this ('this struct if is never closed ... every line after it is skipped silently'), so as written the fragment would swallow the rest of the file. But the two neighbouring examples (lines 1530-1532, 1535-1540) are both closed, so this looks like an example deliberately left open to show the syntax rather than a bug - and doc/superscript.sts is also a functional test that is actually run, where it would matter. I cannot tell which was meant.
